summary: Friedrich August Wolf worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1777–1779) and held a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1783–1807).

Friedrich Bechtel worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen (Ph.D., habilitation), and Strasbourg under Benfey, Fick, Bezzenberger, Windisch, and Scherer. He held posts at Göttingen (from 1878) and Halle (1895–1923).

Friedrich Benedict Weber studied at the University of Leipzig (~1792–1797). He held posts at the University of Frankfurt (Oder) (~1802–1811) and served as professor of political economy at the University of Breslau (~1811–1838).

Friedrich Bollensen worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed a Ph.D. at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald (~1827–1830) and held posts at Gatchina, Saint Petersburg State University (~1842–1856), and Kazan State University as professor of Sanskrit (1852–1856).
Friedrich Brockhaus held professorships at the University of Basel (~1868–1871), Kiel University (~1872–1875), the University of Marburg (~1875–1876), and the University of Jena (~1876–1895).

Andreas worked in Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Halle, Göttingen, Leipzig, Erlangen-Nuremberg, Copenhagen, and Kiel under Pott, von Spiegel, Delitzsch, Ewald, Benfey, and Fleischer, he held posts at the Seminar for Oriental Languages and Göttingen.

Friedrich Carl von Savigny studied at Marburg (~1795–1800), Jena (~1796–1797), and Leipzig (~1797–1798). Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1800–1808) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1842).

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he studied at Heidelberg University (~1849–1851), the University of Paris (~1851–1853), and Trinity College, Cambridge (1852), and studied under Theodor Goldstücker (~1853–1858).

Friedrich Christian Diez worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Giessen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1811–1813) and at the University of Göttingen (~1813–1814), later holding a post at the University of Bonn (~1823–1876).

Friedrich Creuzer worked in religious studies, philosophy, and history/archaeology. He studied at Tübingen (~1789–1791) and Jena (~1791–1794), and held posts at the University of Marburg (~1800–1804), Leiden University (1809), and Heidelberg University (~1804–1845).

Delitzsch worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Jena under Brockhaus, Weber, Fleischer, Dillmann, Schrader, and Curtius. He held professorships at Leipzig (1877), Breslau (1893), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1899).
Friedrich Ernst August Krause worked in sinology. He studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1900–1904) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1923–1942).

Kieckers worked in linguistics, studying at Bonn, Munich, Marburg, Berlin, and Freiburg under Rudolf Thurneysen. He held posts at Freiburg (1911), Munich (1912, 1917), and Tartu as ordinary professor of Indo-European linguistics (1921–1938).

Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at the University of Giessen (~1801–1803), he held posts at Giessen (~1808–1816), the University of Göttingen (~1816–1819), and the University of Bonn (~1819–1861).

Haag worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Zurich, Göttingen, and Berlin under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler and Albrecht Weber. He taught at Zurich, Frauenfeld, Tallinn, Schaffhausen, Burgdorf, and was a professor at the University of Bern (1887–1914).

Heiler worked in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a doctorate at Munich under Hommel, Dyroff, Kieckers, Kuhn, and Scherman. He held posts at Munich (1918, 1962), Greifswald (1934), and Marburg (1920–1962), also directing the Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1927–1962).

Hirth worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Greifswald, and Rostock. He served in the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897) and held the Dean Lung Professorship of Chinese at Columbia University (1902–1917).

Friedrich Karl Ginzel worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an assistant at Sternwarte von Oppolzer (1877–1886) and held a post at the Astronomisches Rechen-Institut beginning in 1886.

Slotty worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Greifswald, Breslau, and Jena under Carl Cappeller and Berthold Delbrück. He held posts at Jena (1912, 1919, 1953–1954), Charles University (1925), and the German University in Prague (1928–1939).

Kluge, a linguist, studied at Leipzig, Strasbourg, and Freiburg under Leskien, Curtius, and Hübschmann. He held posts at the University of Strasbourg (1880), the University of Jena (1884, 1886), and the University of Freiburg as professor of German (1893).
